title: Rillet vs Puzzle: Which Should You Choose?
summary: Discover the key differences between Rillet and Puzzle for your startup's accounting needs. Choose wisely for better financial visibility and automation.
body_markdown:
Are you trying to replace your general ledger, or make startup bookkeeping more continuous? That question separates Rillet from Puzzle more clearly than a long feature checklist. Rillet presents itself as an AI-native ERP and accounting system of record, while Puzzle focuses on automated accounting and financial visibility for startups ([Rillet official website](https://www.rillet.com/) ;[Puzzle official website](https://puzzle.io/) ).


Both products bring automation into transaction processing, reconciliation, reporting, and close workflows. The practical difference is where each product sits, which accounting problems it emphasizes, and how much change your team is prepared to absorb.


## Rillet vs Puzzle at a Glance


Rillet is oriented toward scaling SaaS and subscription companies adopting a new finance system of record, while Puzzle targets startups seeking software-first accounting automation. Rillet emphasizes an AI-native ERP model ([Rillet AI-native ERP guide](https://www.rillet.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-native-erp) ). Puzzle emphasizes automated books and startup financial visibility ([Puzzle official website](https://puzzle.io/) ).


### The Short Answer


Choose Rillet when your finance team is prepared to move onto a new general ledger and needs accounting infrastructure built around SaaS or subscription operations. Its model reaches beyond automating individual bookkeeping tasks because the platform becomes the accounting system itself ([Rillet comparison overview](https://info.rillet.com/rillet-vs-netsuite-intacct-qbo-xero) ).


Choose Puzzle when you want an accessible, startup-oriented accounting platform with automated workflows and visibility into startup financial metrics. Puzzle also positions itself as an alternative to keeping an existing small-business ledger, so migration and control design still belong in the evaluation ([Puzzle QuickBooks comparison](https://puzzle.io/quickbooks) ).

### Key Takeaways


- Rillet fits scaling subscription companies willing to make an AI-native ERP their accounting system of record.
- Puzzle fits startups prioritizing automated bookkeeping, connected banking workflows, and accessible financial visibility.
- Both choices can involve changing the ledger, so migration and control design deserve early attention.
- Teams keeping their current ERP should evaluate an upstream preparation layer as a separate operating model.


## The Most Important Choice Is the Accounting Operating Model


The central decision is whether accounting automation should replace your ledger or prepare work for the ledger you already trust. Rillet explicitly frames itself against established accounting systems ([Rillet comparison overview](https://info.rillet.com/rillet-vs-netsuite-intacct-qbo-xero) ). Puzzle likewise explains its model as an alternative to an existing small-business ledger ([Puzzle QuickBooks comparison](https://puzzle.io/quickbooks) ).


### Replacing the General Ledger Changes the Scope of the Decision


A general-ledger replacement affects more than transaction categorization. Your team must determine how the chart of accounts, historical balances, dimensions, opening data, connected systems, reporting, permissions, approvals, and period-close controls will operate after migration.


That broader scope is not automatically a drawback. If your current ledger no longer fits the company, replacing it may be the right move. But the implementation should be evaluated as a finance-system change, not as a lightweight automation purchase. Rillet’s own comparison material makes that replacement model explicit ([Rillet comparison overview](https://info.rillet.com/rillet-vs-netsuite-intacct-qbo-xero) ).


Puzzle’s software-first approach creates a similar question for startup teams. The product is positioned as more than an add-on to an existing ledger, so buyers should confirm which records move, which integrations become operational dependencies, and how prior-period information will be retained ([Puzzle QuickBooks comparison](https://puzzle.io/quickbooks) ).


### Evaluate Reviewability Alongside Automation


Automation matters only when the accountant can review the resulting work. During an evaluation, ask the vendor to trace a transaction from its original source through classification, reconciliation, adjustment, approval, and the final financial statement.


Use your own accounting examples. Include a changed classification, a missing source file, a split across departments, an unusual balance movement, and a journal entry that requires judgment. The goal is to see whether the system makes those cases visible or simply presents a polished result.


Also test the close artifact itself. A reviewer should be able to determine which source supported the result, what rule was applied, what changed from the prior period, and who approved the final treatment. A dashboard can be useful, but it does not replace support for the work.


## Rillet: An AI-Native General Ledger for Scaling SaaS Companies


Rillet is an AI-native ERP intended to serve as the finance system of record rather than an automation layer attached to another ledger ([Rillet official website](https://www.rillet.com/) ). Its model is aimed at modern finance teams replacing existing accounting systems. That makes it relevant to scaling SaaS and subscription companies prepared for a broader implementation.


### Rillet’s Main Strengths


Rillet’s defining strength is architectural. The general ledger, finance workflows, and automation live in the same product instead of being divided between an established ERP and a separate preparation tool. Rillet describes this model as an AI-native approach to ERP design ([Rillet AI-native ERP guide](https://www.rillet.com/blog/what-is-an-ai-native-erp) ).


That structure can suit a subscription company that wants its revenue workflows and financial reporting inside the new system of record. It also gives the finance team an opportunity to redesign accounting processes instead of preserving every legacy handoff.


Rillet is therefore most relevant when the business has outgrown its current accounting setup and views migration as part of the project. For that buyer, the larger scope can be intentional rather than incidental.


### Rillet’s Limitations and Implementation Tradeoffs


The main tradeoff follows directly from the product model. Adopting Rillet can mean replacing the current ledger, which expands the project to include data migration, integrations, control design, user permissions, reporting continuity, and team adoption ([Rillet comparison overview](https://info.rillet.com/rillet-vs-netsuite-intacct-qbo-xero) ).


Buyers should test the less common work, not just the standard demo. Bring fixed-asset requirements, complex dimensions, unusual revenue arrangements, exports, drill-down expectations, and any inventory or operational accounting needs that matter to your business. Ask the implementation team to show how each case works today.


Ownership matters too. Decide who will validate opening balances, reconcile migrated history, approve the new control design, and support users after launch. A technically capable system can still create friction when those responsibilities remain unclear.


### Rillet Pricing and Overall Value


Rillet directs prospective buyers to its current pricing and packaging process rather than giving this article enough evidence for a universal list price ([Rillet pricing](https://rillet.com/pricing) ). That means a useful comparison should include implementation, migration, configuration, integrations, and ongoing support, not just the subscription quote.


Value depends on whether you actually want a new ERP. If the ledger replacement resolves a broader finance-system problem, the scope may be justified. If your current ledger already meets control and reporting needs, paying for a replacement deserves closer scrutiny.

## Puzzle: Automated Accounting for Startup Finance Stacks


Puzzle is a software-first accounting platform built around automated accounting workflows and financial visibility for startups ([Puzzle official website](https://puzzle.io/) ). It is more accessible in positioning than an enterprise ERP implementation and connects accounting with startup-oriented operating data. For founder-led teams, that focus can make the product easier to evaluate.


### Puzzle’s Main Strengths


Puzzle combines automated accounting with reporting designed for companies that monitor cash, burn, runway, and recurring revenue indicators ([Puzzle official website](https://puzzle.io/) ). That makes it relevant to founders and small finance teams that want accounting information presented in the context of startup operations.


Its banking connectivity is another practical part of the model. Puzzle documents bank integrations as inputs to automated accounting workflows, reducing the separation between financial activity and the accounting platform ([Puzzle banking integrations overview](https://puzzle.io/blog/accounting-software-banking-integrations) ).


Puzzle also speaks directly to startup-focused accounting firms. That audience may value a common software environment for clients with similar banking, card, payroll, billing, and reporting patterns.


### Puzzle’s Limitations and Implementation Tradeoffs


Startup focus can narrow the fit. A team with specialized dimensions, entity-specific allocation rules, extensive multi-currency requirements, or formal reviewer controls should test those workflows with representative data rather than assume startup automation covers them.


Independent evidence is still limited.[The CFO Club’s Puzzle review](https://thecfoclub.com/tools/puzzle-review/) offers one assessment of usability, setup, and buyer fit, but one review should not be treated as a universal account of customer experience.


The practical test is straightforward. Ask Puzzle to process a closed period that includes your real classifications, reconciliations, exceptions, and reviewer questions. Compare the result with the approved books and document every adjustment required.


### Puzzle Pricing and Overall Value


Puzzle publishes current plans and any applicable trial, free-tier, or transaction-volume conditions on its pricing page ([Puzzle pricing](https://puzzle.io/pricing) ). Buyers should verify those terms at the time of purchase because plan boundaries can change.


Its value proposition is strongest when the company wants an accounting platform aligned with startup reporting and a modern finance stack. A controller with more complex entity rules or review requirements should evaluate fit at the workflow level rather than choosing primarily on entry price.


> **How Truewind Is Different** : The upstream model is intended for recurring, reviewer-led preparation in Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online environments. It focuses on the work between source documents and the approved ledger entry rather than replacing the ledger with a startup reporting platform.


## When Truewind Is the Better Fit


Truewind is the better fit when your team wants to preserve Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online while automating recurring accounting preparation. It is designed for nonprofit and mid-market controllers, family-office teams, and CAS practices with source-heavy, reviewer-led workflows. The accountant still owns treatment, corrections, approval, and the final result.


### Keep Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online as the System of Record


The distinction is simple. Truewind sits upstream of the GL. It reads bank statements, processor reports, brokerage statements, PDFs, spreadsheets, and other source materials, then applies the accounting team’s mappings, classifications, dimensions, and prior corrections.


The output is prepared accounting work, including reconciliations, schedules, workpapers, and journal-entry drafts. Reviewers inspect the work, resolve exceptions, make corrections, and approve the result before it moves to the ledger. There is no need to frame automation as autonomous posting.


The upstream model can reduce the scope of change when the existing ERP remains appropriate. If that describes your environment, you can[See Truewind in action](https://www.truewind.ai/see-a-demo?utm_source=oleno&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=rillet-vs-puzzle-which-should-you-choose) using one recurring workflow and its prior approved result.


### Turn Source Documents Into Reviewable Workpapers


Source intake is not merely extraction. The system must determine what a document represents, connect it to the correct entity and account, apply the team’s historical logic, check totals, and show anything that does not fit the expected process.


The workpaper becomes the review surface. It connects the source, calculation, accounting treatment, exceptions, reviewer changes, and approval history. That gives the accountant enough context to understand and re-perform the important steps instead of accepting a clean-looking output without support.


Start with a bounded workflow that has known inputs and an approved answer. A prepaid schedule, processor reconciliation, brokerage rollforward, or donation reconciliation can provide a concrete comparison point. ## Rillet vs Puzzle: How to Make the Final Choice


The final choice should follow your desired accounting operating model, company stage, and review requirements. Choose Rillet when adopting a new system of record supports a scaling SaaS finance function. Choose Puzzle when startup-focused automation and financial visibility matter most, then evaluate an upstream preparation layer if preserving your current ledger is non-negotiable.

Rillet makes sense when the company wants to redesign accounting around a new AI-native general ledger. Puzzle makes sense when a startup wants automated accounting and financial visibility shaped around its operating metrics. Neither selection should be made from the feature list alone.


If you want to keep your current ledger, use the same evaluation discipline on the upstream work. Bring a source set, prior workpaper, approved journal entry, known exceptions, and named reviewer. Then ask the vendor to reproduce the workflow and show every handoff. ## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do I choose between Rillet and Puzzle?


To choose between Rillet and Puzzle, consider your company's needs: 1) If you're scaling a SaaS or subscription business and need a new general ledger, Rillet is your best fit. 2) If you're a startup looking for automated accounting and financial visibility, Puzzle may be more suitable. 3) Evaluate if you're ready to migrate to a new system or if you prefer to keep your existing ledger while enhancing your accounting processes.


### What if I want to keep my current general ledger?


If you want to keep your current general ledger, consider using Truewind. It integrates with systems like Sage Intacct or QuickBooks Online, allowing you to automate recurring accounting preparation without replacing your GL. This way, you can maintain your existing setup while still improving efficiency in your accounting workflows.


### When should I consider migrating to a new finance system?


Consider migrating to a new finance system like Rillet when your current ledger no longer meets your business needs, especially if you're scaling and require a more robust accounting infrastructure. Evaluate your team's readiness for change and ensure you have a clear plan for data migration, integration, and user training to facilitate a smooth transition.


### Why does accounting automation need human review?


Accounting automation requires human review to ensure accuracy and compliance. While systems like Truewind can prepare work and surface exceptions, the final judgment and approval should come from accountants. This ensures that any discrepancies or unusual items are properly addressed and that the financial statements reflect the team's standards and practices.
